summary: A form backend for static sites: point any plain HTML form at your endpoint and get the submission stored, emailed to you and optionally posted to a webhook, with a honeypot, rate limits and an origin allowlist so strangers cannot post to it. Static site stays static; you run one small server.

stack.why: a dead mail host must never lose a submission
the endpoint must be public HTTPS

prerequisites.name: Node.js 22 or newer
prerequisites.why: Everything in this build runs on it: the server, the scripts, the tests.
prerequisites.get: Download the LTS installer from nodejs.org, or install with your package manager (brew install node, or nvm install 22). Restart the terminal afterwards.

prerequisites.name: A terminal and a code editor
prerequisites.why: Every step below is a command you type or a file you edit.
prerequisites.get: VS Code (code.visualstudio.com), Cursor or Zed. Open a folder for the project and use the editor's built-in terminal.
prerequisites.verify: You can open a folder and run a command in its terminal

prerequisites.name: Git
prerequisites.why: History for your code, and the way most hosts deploy.
prerequisites.get: Install from git-scm.com or with your package manager, then run git init in the project folder once it exists.

prerequisites.name: The static sites whose forms will post here, with their origins
prerequisites.why: Phase 2 refuses any origin not in the allowlist.
prerequisites.get: List each site's https origin exactly.

prerequisites.name: SMTP credentials for notifications
prerequisites.get: Fastmail, Postmark, Resend SMTP or your mail host: host, port, user, app password.

prerequisites.name: A small always-on server (VPS)
prerequisites.why: This needs one process running all the time with a public address.
prerequisites.get: Hetzner Cloud (from about 4 EUR), DigitalOcean or Fly.io. Ubuntu 24.04, the smallest size. You need SSH access and a public IP. Only needed for the deploy phase; develop locally first.

prerequisites.name: A domain or subdomain
prerequisites.why: A public address you own, so links you share never break when a provider changes.
prerequisites.get: Register at Cloudflare Registrar, Porkbun or Namecheap, or use a subdomain of one you already own. You add one DNS record in the deploy phase.
prerequisites.cost: roughly $10 a year, or free on an existing domain

prerequisites.name: Caddy on the server
prerequisites.why: Automatic HTTPS in front of the Node process. Without TLS the browser features this relies on (and your visitors' trust) do not work.
prerequisites.get: On the VPS: follow the install steps at caddyserver.com/docs/install for Ubuntu. One Caddyfile with your domain and a reverse_proxy line is the whole config.
prerequisites.verify: caddy version prints a version on the server

env.name: ADMIN_USER
env.where: Any username for the basic-auth admin pages.

env.name: ADMIN_PASS
env.where: Generate one: openssl rand -base64 24. Never reuse a real password.

phases.title: Accept a post
phases.goal: A plain HTML form on another site submits and lands on a thank-you.

steps.detail: forms (id, slug, name, redirect_url, notify_email, webhook_url), submissions (id, form_id, received_at, fields JSON, ip_hash, user_agent_class, spam). Fields as JSON because you do not control the markup that posts to you.
commands: mkdir formback && cd formback && git init && npm init -y && npm pkg set type=module

steps.do: Implement POST /f/:slug for urlencoded and multipart text fields, 64 kB cap, 303 to redirect_url or a plain thank-you; JSON when the Accept header asks

check: A blank HTML page's form submits with JavaScript disabled and lands on the thank-you
One row with the fields intact

phases.title: Spam controls
phases.goal: Honeypot, rate limit, origin allowlist, bot filter, all flagging rather than deleting.

steps.do: Honeypot field _gotcha: filled means store with spam true and redirect normally
Per-IP limit of 10 per hour in SQLite; refuse origins not in ALLOWED_ORIGINS; coarse bot user-agent filter

check: A filled honeypot redirects and stores a spam row
The eleventh post in an hour is refused

phases.title: Notifications
phases.goal: Email and webhook that never make the visitor wait.

steps.do: Send an email over SMTP_URL with the fields as a table, fire-and-forget with a timeout
POST the JSON to webhook_url when set, same rules

check: A submission stores and redirects with SMTP unreachable
A real send arrives readable on a phone

phases.title: File uploads
phases.goal: Safe uploads with a generated name and a streaming cap.

steps.do: Stream multipart files to UPLOAD_DIR/<slug>/ with a 10 MB cap while streaming and a MIME sniff
Strip EXIF from images and never web-serve UPLOAD_DIR directly

check: An 11 MB file is refused before it is fully read

phases.title: Admin
phases.goal: Forms, the snippet, submissions with spam separate, CSV.

steps.do: Basic-auth /admin: create forms and copy the paste-in HTML snippet with the honeypot field
Submissions per form with a spam tab, restore-from-spam, and streamed CSV

check: A form goes from created to a real submission using only the snippet
A 10,000-row export does not grow memory

phases.title: Deploy

steps.do: /healthz, systemd, Caddy, nightly backup of data/
README: the snippet verbatim, the allowlist step, where data lives

check: A restore brings back rows and files
The README reaches a working form

phases.title: Operate it like a product
phases.goal: Only for the product-builder path: know when the endpoint is down, never lose the database, and keep the server patched.

steps.do: Add a /healthz endpoint and an external uptime check against it
steps.detail: Answer 200 with the build id and a quick database read. Point a free uptime monitor (or your own, from the Healthchecks entry on this site) at it so an outage is noticed before a user notices.

steps.do: Write structured request logs and rotate them
steps.detail: One JSON line per request: method, path, status, duration, no raw IPs. Rotate weekly with logrotate, keep eight.

steps.do: Back the SQLite file up off the machine nightly and test a restore
steps.detail: SQLite's .backup command makes a consistent copy while the app runs. Copy it to object storage or a second machine; then, once, restore it into a fresh checkout and confirm the app reads it.
Firewall allowing only 22, 80 and 443; unattended security updates on; the app running as an unprivileged user under systemd with Restart=on-failure.

check: Stopping the service triggers an uptime alert within a few minutes
A restore from last night's backup contains yesterday's data
A port scan from another machine shows only 22, 80 and 443

product.outcome: A form backend for every static site you ship, with spam flagged not lost and notifications that cannot break a submission.

architecture.swap: Any handler writing the same rows
Object storage behind the same functions

operations.backup: tar of data/ nightly off the box.
operations.monitoring: Uptime on /healthz; a spike in spam rows.
operations.incident: Spam wave: tighten limits, tag the pattern. Leaked SMTP: rotate.

notIncluded: The integrations gallery and hosted file storage.
Spam filtering tuned on someone else's traffic.
Not running a server, which is what Formspree actually sells.
after: Per-form autoresponder email to the submitter
